requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: After a successful AUTH command completes, a server MUST reject any further AUTH commands with a 503 reply.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: An AUTH command issued during a mail transaction MUST be rejected with a 503 reply.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the server supports the [ESMTP-CODES] extension, it SHOULD return a 5.5.4 enhanced response code.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the server receives such a response, it MUST reject the AUTH command by sending a 501 reply.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the initial response argument is omitted and the chosen mechanism requires an initial client response, the server MUST proceed as defined in Section 5.1 of [SASL].

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If use of the initial response argument would cause the AUTH command to exceed this length, the client MUST NOT use the initial response parameter (and instead proceed as defined in Section 5.1 of [SASL]).

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the client is transmitting an initial response of zero length, it MUST instead transmit the response as a single equals sign ("=").

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Servers using the enhanced status codes extension [ESMTP-CODES] SHOULD return an enhanced status code of 5.7.0 in this case.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the server cannot [BASE64] decode any client response, it MUST reject the AUTH command with a 501 reply (and an enhanced status code of 5.5.2).

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the client cannot BASE64 decode any of the server's challenges, it MUST cancel the authentication using the "*" response.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: In particular, servers and clients MUST reject (and not ignore) any character not explicitly allowed by the BASE64 alphabet, and MUST reject any sequence of BASE64 characters that contains the pad character ('=') anywhere other than the end of the string (e.g., "=AAA" and "AAA=BBB" are not allowed).

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Clients and servers MUST be able to handle the maximum encoded size of challenges and responses generated by their supported authentication mechanisms.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Servers using the enhanced status codes extension [ESMTP-CODES] SHOULD return an enhanced status code of 5.5.6 in this case.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: The authorization identity generated by this [SASL] exchange is a "simple username" (in the sense defined in [SASLprep]), and both client and server SHOULD (*) use the [SASLprep] profile of the [StringPrep] algorithm to prepare these names for transmission or comparison.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If preparation of the authorization identity fails or results in an empty string (unless it was transmitted as the empty string), the server MUST fail the authentication.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: (*) Note: Future revision of this specification may change this requirement to MUST.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Currently, the SHOULD is used in order to avoid breaking the majority of existing implementations.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If the server is unable to authenticate the client, it SHOULD reject the AUTH command with a 535 reply unless a more specific error code is appropriate.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: The server MUST discard any knowledge obtained from the client, such as the EHLO argument, which was not obtained from the SASL negotiation itself.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Likewise, the client MUST discard any knowledge obtained from the server, such as the list of SMTP service extensions, which was not obtained from the SASL negotiation itself.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: (Note that a client MAY compare the advertised SASL mechanisms before and after authentication in order to detect an active down- negotiation attack).

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: The client SHOULD send an EHLO command as the first command after a successful SASL negotiation that results in the enabling of a security layer.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: When an entity (whether it is the client or the server end) is sending data, and both [TLS] and SASL security layers are in effect, the TLS encoding MUST be applied after the SASL encoding, regardless of the order in which the layers were negotiated.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: If an AUTH command fails, the client MAY proceed without authentication.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Alternatively, the client MAY try another authentication mechanism or present different credentials by issuing another AUTH

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Note: A server implementation MUST implement a configuration in which it does NOT permit any plaintext password mechanisms, unless either the STARTTLS [SMTP-TLS] command has been negotiated or some other mechanism that protects the session from password snooping has been provided.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: Server sites SHOULD NOT use any configuration which permits a plaintext password mechanism without such a protection mechanism against password snooping.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: To ensure interoperability, client and server implementations of this extension MUST implement the [PLAIN] SASL mechanism running over TLS [TLS] [SMTP-TLS].

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: In order to ensure interoperability with deployed software, new implementations MAY implement it; however, implementations should be aware that this SASL mechanism doesn't provide any server authentication.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Command
requirements.text: When the AUTH command is used together with the [PIPELINING] extension, it MUST be the last command in a pipelined group of commands.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: If the server trusts the authenticated identity of the client to assert that the message was originally submitted by the supplied <mailbox>, then the server SHOULD supply the same <mailbox> in an AUTH parameter when relaying the message to any other server which supports the AUTH extension.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: For this reason, servers that advertise support for this extension MUST support the AUTH parameter to the MAIL FROM command even when the client has not authenticated itself to the server.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: The server MUST NOT treat the message as having been originally submitted by the authenticated identity that resulted from the AUTH command.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: If the AUTH parameter to the MAIL FROM command is not supplied, the client has authenticated, and the server believes the message is an original submission, the server MAY generate a <mailbox> from the user's authenticated identity for use in an AUTH parameter when relaying the message to any server which supports the AUTH extension.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: The generated <mailbox> is implementation specific, but it MUST conform to the syntax of [SMTP].

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: If the implementation cannot generate a valid <mailbox>, it MUST transmit AUTH=<> when relaying this message.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: If the server does not sufficiently trust the authenticated identity of the client, or if the client is not authenticated, then the server MUST behave as if the AUTH=<> parameter was supplied.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: The server MAY, however, write the value of any supplied AUTH parameter to a log file.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: If an AUTH=<> parameter was supplied, either explicitly or due to the requirement in the previous paragraph, then the server MUST supply the AUTH=<> parameter when relaying the message to any server which it has authenticated to using the AUTH extension.

requirements.heading: The AUTH Parameter to the MAIL FROM command
requirements.text: A server MAY treat expansion of a mailing list as a new submission, setting the AUTH parameter to the mailing list address or mailing list administration address when relaying the message to list subscribers.

requirements.heading: Status Codes
requirements.text: The client SHOULD retry with a new authentication mechanism.

requirements.heading: Status Codes
requirements.text: In this case, the client SHOULD ask the user to supply new credentials (such as by presenting a password dialog box).

requirements.text: This response SHOULD be returned by any command other than AUTH, EHLO, HELO, NOOP, RSET, or QUIT when server policy requires authentication in order to perform the requested action and authentication is not currently in force.

requirements.text: This enhanced status code SHOULD be returned when the server fails the AUTH command due to the client sending a [BASE64] response which is longer than the maximum buffer size available for the currently selected SASL mechanism.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements on Servers
requirements.text: As described in Section 4.4 of [SMTP], an SMTP server that receives a message for delivery or further processing MUST insert the "Received:" header field at the beginning of the message content.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements on Servers
requirements.text: Upon successful authentication, a server SHOULD use the "ESMTPA" or the "ESMTPSA" [SMTP-TT] (when appropriate) keyword in the "with" clause of the Received header field.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: For this reason, clients and servers MUST discard any knowledge obtained prior to the start of the SASL negotiation upon the establishment of a security layer.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: Servers MAY implement a policy whereby the connection is dropped after a number of failed authentication attempts.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: If they do so, they SHOULD NOT drop the connection until at least 3 attempts to authenticate have failed.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: If an implementation supports SASL mechanisms that are vulnerable to passive eavesdropping attacks (such as [PLAIN]), then the implementation MUST support at least one configuration where these SASL mechanisms are not advertised or used without the presence of an external security layer such as [TLS].

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements When Using SASL PLAIN over TLS
requirements.text: If the server has not provided any certificate, or if the certificate verification fails, the client MUST NOT attempt to authenticate using the SASL PLAIN mechanism.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements When Using SASL PLAIN over TLS
requirements.text: After a successful [TLS] negotiation, the client MUST check its understanding of the server hostname against the server's identity as presented in the server Certificate message, in order to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements When Using SASL PLAIN over TLS
requirements.text: If the match fails, the client MUST NOT attempt to authenticate using the SASL PLAIN mechanism.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements When Using SASL PLAIN over TLS
requirements.text: The client MUST use the server hostname it used to open the connection as the value to compare against the server name as expressed in the server certificate.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements When Using SASL PLAIN over TLS
requirements.text: If a subjectAltName extension of type dNSName is present in the certificate, it SHOULD be used as the source of the server's identity.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements When Using SASL PLAIN over TLS
requirements.text: A "*" wildcard character MAY be used as the leftmost name component in the certificate.

requirements.heading: Changes since RFC 2554
requirements.text: Clarified that servers MUST support the use of the AUTH=mailbox parameter to MAIL FROM, even when the client is not authenticated.
